source_text.body:
Draft support ticket responses from research
A support engineer uses n8n to research customer tickets, draft final responses, and learn from closed tickets to improve future troubleshooting.
·
Jul 19, 2025
Done with
N8
n8n
What they did
A remote support engineer ran n8n on a localhost office PC to add private notes to support tickets, do initial research, search the web and an internal database, and draft a customer reply. For recurring issues it suggested faster responses, but a human still finalized them; after successful closes, resolved tickets were sent into a database when no similar document already existed so the system could learn troubleshooting patterns.
How it went
They said it already saves about 50% of the work on customer answers and they hope that grows to 75% as the database expands. They also built a tech-sheet ingester that took about 10 minutes per document across 20 documents, produced roughly 2,500 vectors, and was checked as about 99% correct.
Worth knowing
The main catch was build effort: they said they spent a lot of time programming it and learning prompting before the time savings kicked in.
Try it yourself
with
n8n
Copy prompt
Build an n8n workflow that triggers when a new support ticket arrives in [helpdesk tool]. It should search [knowledge base, docs, past closed tickets] for relevant fixes, then draft a reply for the customer and add it as an internal note. When a ticket closes, store the problem and solution so future drafts can use it. Never send a reply to a customer automatically; show me each draft for approval first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/n8n/comments/1m3q7tf/is_there_any_people_on_this_rn8n_automating
